question.text: Mr. Vivek Saxena, a high-income resident LP, receives pass-through LTCG of INR 5 crore on unlisted shares from Krishna Private Equity Fund (Cat II). Mr. Saxena's total income puts him in the peak surcharge bracket (which would otherwise be 37%). Under the post-Budget 2022 rules, what is the surcharge rate applicable on the LTCG component?

answer.text: 15% (capped at 15% for LTCG and certain STCG).

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the post-Finance-Act-2022 position, surcharge on long-term capital gains under Sections 112/112A (and on STCG under Section 111A for listed equity on which STT is paid) is capped at 15%, even where the taxpayer's other income would otherwise attract a higher 25% or 37% surcharge slab. So Mr. Saxena's INR 5 crore LTCG on unlisted shares is taxed at the applicable LTCG base rate plus a 15% (capped) surcharge plus 4% cess. The peak 37% surcharge continues to apply to his other (non-capital-gains) income. The Trap: Option A applies the peak surcharge to LTCG, ignoring the 15% cap. Option B is an intermediate surcharge slab. Option D is below the prescribed cap. Note: The XIX-D workbook supports unlisted-share LTCG taxation at 12.5% plus applicable surcharge and cess, but the specific post-Budget-2022 15% surcharge cap for LTCG/STCG-on-111A is not stated in the cited workbook pages. The surcharge cap should be cross-checked against the current Income-tax Act and Finance Act amendments.
